## 2. Statement of Facts

The Assessing Officer issued a notice under the erstwhile Section 148 on 15 April 2021 for Assessment Year 2018-19. The Company contends the notice is time-barred and was issued under a provision already substituted by the Finance Act, 2021, effective 1 April 2021.

## 3. Issue for Consideration

Whether the reassessment notice for AY 2018-19 is valid, having regard to the transition from the old to the new reassessment regime and the Supreme Court's rulings in Ashish Agarwal and Rajeev Bansal.

## 4. Relevant Legal Framework

- Section 147
- Section 148
- Section 148A
- Section 149
- TOLA, 2020


## 5. Judicial Precedents Considered

- Union of India v. Ashish Agarwal, (2022) 444 ITR 1 (SC)
- Union of India v. Rajeev Bansal (2024) (SC)

## 6. Analysis

Following Ashish Agarwal, notices issued under the old Section 148 between 1 April and 30 June 2021 are deemed to be show-cause notices under Section 148A(b) of the new regime. Rajeev Bansal further clarified that the time available to the Assessing Officer to complete the Section 148A procedure and issue a fresh notice stood extended by the surviving period under TOLA, 2020. Validity for AY 2018-19 will therefore turn on strict compliance with the resultant procedural timeline, and on whether escaped income exceeds the INR 50 lakh threshold required to justify the extended (up to 10-year) limitation period under Section 149.

## 7. Conclusion / Opinion

The validity of the notice is fact-dependent on demonstrable compliance with the post-Ashish Agarwal/Rajeev Bansal procedural timeline and the applicable monetary threshold; a writ challenge has a reasonable, though not assured, prospect of success.

**Confidence level:** Fairly arguable
